newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes just easier as dollar holds dip.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes just easier as dollar holds dip.

text.p: Precious metals prices were narrowly mixed on Wednesday afternoon after the dollar held a dip, and an early rise in New York was sold into, dealers said.
They said there were no fresh factors in the market to suggest a move above the current $337.00-$340.00 per ounce.
Gold was fixed at $338.45 just 25 cents under the morning fixing and 10 cents up on Tuesday afternoon.
The August Comex contract was up $0.60 at $340.30 at the fix having gained over a dollar in early business.

The dollar held against the mark and yen after dipping briefly and adding a few cents to the gold price after U.S. May durable good orders indicated a slowing in the domestic economy with an unexpected drop of 0.6 percent.
The fixing confirmed the moribund state of the market since it found physical buying support on Monday to rescue it from a plunge towards four year lows.
"There is good support from a reasonable level of physical offtake but the producers will sell into any sort of rally," a dealer said.
"This could be the pattern for some time to come," he added.
Silver edged a cent firmer but couldn't hold that to remain unchanged at $4.77/$4.79.

"There isn't the overhang of central bank selling potential for silver and the fundamentals are relatively positive. But it has failed on the upside three times recently and seems to be anchored by gold," a dealer said.
Platinum and palladium were both virtually unchanged and ignored comments from South African producer Amplats estimating Russian platinum shipments this year to be down 42.6 percent.
Managing director Barry Davison forecast shipments of 700,000 ounces this year against 1.22 million ounces in 1996.
Possibly more significantly Davison stated that the South African producers -- the world leaders -- would produce probably less than the 3,645,000 ounces they had forecast for 1997.
Russia has not exported either platinum or palladium this year due to administrative problems.
Officials in Moscow stated this week that 1997 exports due to begin later this month would be down on last year's level.
Russia is the leading exporter of palladium and is second to South Africa in platinum shipments.
Platinum was $2.00 firmer at $413.50/$418.50 and palladium unchanged at $195.00/$200.00.
